questions.stem: A thrust block's job is to:
options: Cool the shaft where it leaves the hull
Measure shaft speed for the tachometer
Pass propeller thrust from the shaft to the hull
Reduce propeller noise and vibration
questions.explanation: It stops the shaft from pushing the engine and carries thrust to the hull.

questions.stem: A water-lubricated stern gland with packing normally:
options: Drips slightly, so it stays cool without much leakage
Should be tightened until it is completely dry, with no drip
Should never be touched once it is set up
Should leak freely to keep the shaft cool
questions.explanation: A slight drip keeps packing cool. Over-tightening can overheat the gland and shaft.

questions.stem: Before starting a vessel's engine and gearbox, a basic check on the gearbox is:
options: Galley fuel stock
Anchor light and deck light function
Radio channel setting
Oil level and condition
questions.explanation: Low or contaminated gearbox oil damages gears and bearings.

questions.stem: Theoretical propeller pitch is the distance a propeller would advance:
options: In one minute
In one tide
In one nautical mile
In one revolution
questions.explanation: Pitch is like the thread pitch of a screw.

questions.stem: The correct order of the drive line from engine to water on a single-screw vessel is:
options: Gearbox, engine, coupling, propeller, shaft, stern gland
Engine, coupling, gearbox, shaft, stern gland, propeller
Engine, propeller, shaft, gearbox, coupling, stern gland
Stern gland, shaft, engine, gearbox, coupling, propeller
questions.explanation: Power goes from the engine through a flexible coupling and gearbox, down the shaft, out through the stern tube and gland to the propeller.

questions.stem: An engine turns at 1 800 rpm through a 2:1 reduction gearbox. The propeller shaft speed is:
options: 3 600 rpm
1 800 rpm
900 rpm
600 rpm
questions.explanation: Shaft speed = engine speed divided by ratio = 1 800 / 2 = 900 rpm.

questions.stem: When changing from ahead to astern with a marine gearbox you should:
options: Move the lever quickly at full revolutions
Reduce to idle and pause in neutral before engaging astern
Stop the engine first, then restart
Engage astern before reducing speed so the propeller stops quickly
questions.explanation: Shifting at idle with a pause in neutral protects the clutches and gears from shock.

questions.stem: A propeller of pitch 0.8 m turns at 500 rpm and the vessel makes 9.72 knots (theoretical speed 12.96 knots). The slip is about:
options: 25 per cent
12 per cent
3 per cent
75 per cent
questions.explanation: Slip = (12.96 - 9.72) / 12.96 = 0.25, or 25 per cent. Some slip is normal.

questions.stem: The whole vessel starts to vibrate at a certain engine speed. A reasonable thing to check is:
options: The galley stove and its fuel line
The fresh-water tank level
The radar mast and its scanner
The propeller, coupling, shaft line and cutless bearing
questions.explanation: Bent or fouled propellers, misalignment and worn bearings all cause shaft-line vibration.
